rules.title: Implicit prelude auto-imported per file
rules.statement: Every source file implicitly imports the prelude package in addition to its explicit `use` declarations, unless the file opts out. The implicit prelude is deduplicated against explicit uses (no duplicate import if already named).
rules.divergence: Logos uses a named prelude *package*; the model parallels Rust's std prelude but is package-granular.

rules.title: #![no_implicit_prelude] suppresses implicit prelude
rules.statement: A file-level inner attribute `#![no_implicit_prelude]` suppresses the implicit prelude import for that file. It is recognized as an INNER_ANNOTATION item with name `no_implicit_prelude`.

rules.title: Dotted use path
rules.statement: `use a.b.c;` names the package whose dotted path is the concatenation of the head identifier and successive `.`-separated path parts: `a.b.c`. Package paths use `.` as the separator.

rules.title: use group desugars to N imports
rules.statement: `use pkg.{a, b, c};` (USE_GROUP / USE_VARIANTS form) desugars to N separate package imports, one per group member, where each lowercase-leading group prefix forms a sub-package: `use pkg.sub.{a,b}` yields imports `pkg.sub.a`, `pkg.sub.b`.

rules.title: Group target classified by first-character case
rules.statement: In a USE_VARIANTS group `use pkg.X.{...};`, the bracketed target `X` is classified by its first character: lowercase-leading `X` is treated as a grouped sub-package import (each member becomes `pkg.X.<member>`); uppercase-leading `X` is treated as an enum-variant import, importing the enclosing package `pkg` as a wildcard so the type is in scope. This relies on the convention that enum/type names are capitalized.
rules.divergence: Disambiguation by identifier capitalization is a Logos convention, not a Rust rule.

rules.title: Package-level dependency cycles are legal
rules.statement: Cyclic `use` dependencies between packages are legal (e.g. option <-> result, where each package's methods reference the other). Mutually-dependent packages form a strongly-connected component and are compiled together.

rules.title: Modules processed dependencies-first
rules.statement: Modules are ordered so that for any `use`-edge from package u to package v, v is processed before u. Ordering is package-granular: all files of a package move together, preserving first-seen order within a package and within an SCC; absent a forcing dep edge, original load order is preserved (stable).

rules.title: package declaration
rules.statement: A file's package is declared by a leading `package <dotted-ident>;` statement, where `<dotted-ident>` is a sequence of `[A-Za-z0-9_.]` characters. The declaration may be preceded only by comments, blank lines, and inner attribute lines (`#![...]`); the first non-trivia token must be `package` or the file has no package declaration.

rules.title: `use pkg from <module>` clause: operand syntax and extraction
rules.statement: The optional `from <module>` clause of a `use` names the providing module as its operand. The operand may be a bare identifier or a double-quoted string literal; surrounding quotes are stripped to yield the module name. Absence of the `from` clause records an empty module name, selecting default resolution. The clause is recorded as a (package dotted-path, from-module) pair.
rules.divergence: Logos-specific: type/package coexistence across modules sharing a package name (no Rust analog).
